nodes.label: Assignment project brief
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: A 6-week individual or pair project for Network Application Development. Students build a distributed streaming client-server collaboration application. Suggested deadline is Sunday, November 17, 2026, 11:59 PM, submitted as a zip or a private GitHub repository.

nodes.label: Self-hosted collaboration need
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Slack, Microsoft Teams, and cloud storage send data through third-party servers, which raises privacy, compliance, and bandwidth concerns on closed networks. The brief asks for a lightweight secure self-hosted application so people on the same LAN or VPN can talk and share files without external infrastructure. Target users are air-gapped corporate teams, student groups without internet, and people who want self-hosted tools.

nodes.label: User authentication and discovery
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md

nodes.label: Streaming broadcast and unicast messaging
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: The brief requires broadcast global chat and unicast private messages, and points at Steam GameNetworkingSockets and Google QUIC as message-oriented transport references. Reliable delivery is required because it is a messaging application.

nodes.label: Reliable file transfer requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Step 6 requires chunking, reassembly over UDP, and no corruption for files of various formats and sizes.

nodes.label: Connection resilience requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md

nodes.label: Payload encryption requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Basic encryption of payloads, for example AES, or TLS sockets, to resist packet sniffing. Step 8 scores encrypt-before-send and decrypt-on-receipt with a standard crypto library.

nodes.label: Raw sockets only constraint
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Flask, Django, WebSockets, and other high-level networking libraries are prohibited so students practice raw sockets (Python socket, java.net.Socket, and the equivalents). Languages suggested are Python, Java, C++, or Go. The program must run on Windows, macOS, or Linux over localhost or a LAN IP.

nodes.label: Head-of-line blocking requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Time-sensitive streaming must fetch data asynchronously. UDP streaming carries byte chunks only; application-layer protocol logic has to remove head-of-line blocking. The server should handle about 10 to 20 concurrent clients.

nodes.label: Sliding window sequencing
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Monotonic sequence numbers and a window provide flow control and in-order delivery.

nodes.label: Selective retransmission
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md

nodes.label: BBR and CUBIC requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Streaming congestion control must support BBR or CUBIC.

nodes.label: TCP reliable path and UDP discovery
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: The techniques section asks for TCP for reliable file and message transfer and UDP for heartbeat and discovery broadcasts. Step 2 separately asks for a basic TCP handshake and acknowledgement, while step 6 asks for file reassembly over UDP. Those two steps do not name the same transport.

nodes.label: Ten-step grading rubric
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Ten milestones, one point each: protocol design, handshake, authentication and state, concurrency, message routing, reliable file transfer, resilience, encryption, an HTTP UI with client-side JavaScript only, and tests plus code quality. The UI may be a CLI or a GUI but must show network status. Network logic, data processing, and the interface must be separated.

nodes.label: HTTP UI with client-side JavaScript
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Step 9 requires a friendly interface that shows incoming messages, file-transfer progress, and the active user list, built with HTTP and client-side JavaScript only.

nodes.label: Concurrency requirement
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Multi-threading or asynchronous I/O so many clients can connect and disconnect without blocking the main thread.

nodes.label: Custom application-layer protocol
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Step 1 requires the packet layout, message types such as AUTH, MSG, and FILE, and state diagrams in documentation before coding. Serialization may be JSON, XML, or a custom binary packing. Submission also requires an architecture diagram, a protocol specification, sequence diagrams for a message and a file transfer, and a one-page challenges-and-solutions reflection.

nodes.label: TCP client-server handshake step
nodes.source_file: graphify-out/converted/Assignment 1 - Distributed Streaming-based Client-Server Collaboration Application_1fd07668.md
nodes.rationale: Step 2 is worded as a basic TCP socket connection in which the client connects and receives an acknowledgement.
